$schema: component-compatibility.schema (informal) — see COMPONENT_COMPATIBILITY_MATRIX milestone report for classification rules

classificationLegend.A: FULL RUNTIME + INTERACTIVE — simulation mapping + compatible pins + runtime model + realtime input capability confirmed by RuntimeCapabilityResolver AND wired to ISimulationInputChannel
classificationLegend.B: RUNTIME OUTPUT — real runtime model exists (either runner), component reacts to program logic, no live user input
classificationLegend.C: WIRING VALIDATION — dedicated pin/wiring rule (Require() checks) exists, no runtime behavior in either runner
classificationLegend.D: VISUAL ONLY — renders on canvas; either only the generic structural-only wiring warning applies, or no SupportedPins entry exists at all
classificationLegend.E: IMPORTED / NOT MAPPED — present in Component Registry (Fritzing/KiCad import) but SimulationComponentType is null

visualCapabilityLegend.REAL_PROVIDER_VISUAL: Real, verified external visual asset depicting the actual physical component, with real pin geometry from that same source (today: exclusively @wokwi/elements — Fritzing/KiCad have never produced a usable visual asset, see REAL COMPONENT VISUAL milestone Checkpoint A). Independent of simulation/runtime status.
visualCapabilityLegend.VERIFIED_INTERNAL_VISUAL: A hand-built StemFlow illustration that has been checked against a real reference (photo/datasheet) for shape, connector grouping, and pin placement — not photorealistic, but not a meaningless placeholder either. Added in the VISUAL REFINEMENT / EXPANSION phase: most of these SVGs already existed and were already reference-accurate, they had just never been formally assessed against the matrix.
visualCapabilityLegend.GENERIC_FALLBACK: A clean, honestly-generic card/shape — never claims to depict the real physical component. Pin NAMES may still be verified (see pinDefinitionVerified) even when the visual itself is generic.

FIXED 2026-08-23 (was 'blocked by a real, narrow compile-contract bug' — see git history for the prior write-up). A real scripted-sensor runtime model exists in source for QEMU: SensorRuntimeHeaderGenerator.cs (Dht22Type/Dht11Type) reads sensorScenario timeline from diagram JSON and generates a StemFlowDHT C++ class (readTemperature/readHumidity, step-function lookup by millis()), injected into the compiled firmware by FirmwareCacheService (gated by SimulationRunner:Qemu:EnableSensorInputScenario=true in appsettings.json). The previously-broken contract (student code writes '#include "StemFlowDHT.h"', but no such file existed in the compile sandbox — 'fatal error: StemFlowDHT.h: No such file or directory') is now fixed: SensorRuntimeHeaderGenerator.BuildExtraFiles() emits a real (intentionally empty, include-guard only) StemFlowDHT.h stub whenever a DHT11/DHT22 component is present, threaded through CompileSimulationRequest.ExtraFiles and written into the sketch sandbox by SimulationCompileService alongside sketch.ino — the actual class keeps coming from the existing inlined text earlier in the same sketch.ino. Live-verified end-to-end via a real Docker/arduino-cli compile + real QEMU run of the exact Bai 10 sample exercise and its sensorScenario timeline (25C/55% -> 30C/50% -> 38C/40% -> 26C/58%): compile succeeded, Serial Monitor printed the exact temperature/humidity sequence, LED (GPIO13) went HIGH only during the 38C sample and correctly printed 'CANH BAO: NHIET DO CAO!', then returned LOW — confirming Sensor Scenario data genuinely flows through the real compiled firmware into student code, not simulated/faked at any layer. Classification upgraded C -> B (RUNTIME OUTPUT: real runtime model, reacts to program logic, no live user input — scenario is baked in at compile time).
